text:
- chief complaint: the patient was referred for an evaluation of abnormal lab work showing low immunoglobulin A (IgA) levels, prompting anxiety about the finding.
- history of present illness: the referral followed a routine physical; the patient reports frequent colds that linger, but is unsure whether this exceeds baseline. No family history of immune deficiency, no recent blood transfusions, and a recent international trip to Zambia that disqualified them from donating blood.
- physical examination: vitals unremarkable, no fever, regular heart rhythm without murmurs, clear lungs, no cervical lymphadenopathy, and a soft, non-tender abdomen.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: frequent upper respiratory infections (colds that linger); no abdominal infections or severe diarrhea reported.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: metformin, started by the PCP for newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes; dosage N/A.
- follow-up instructions: additional blood work to check other antibodies; report persistent or hard-to-control infections, abdominal changes, or severe diarrhea; inform clinicians of IgA deficiency before any blood product transfusion.
